need: stop the built-in antivirus from conflicting with the antimalware suite the company has standardized on
clues: the company has licensed a third-party antimalware suite for every PC
two scanners running at once slow the PCs and lock files
the third-party suite has been installed and is up to date
the change is made from Manage settings under Virus and threat protection

answer.item: Turning off real-time protection in Microsoft Defender Antivirus

appliesWhen: a separate antimalware product must protect the PC without the built-in scanner getting in its way
explanation: Real-time protection can be switched off in Manage settings so that Defender does not conflict with another antimalware product. At least one antimalware product must stay active on the PC.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

need: make sure the built-in antivirus can recognize the newest threats
clues: the laptop has been switched off in a drawer for three months
the Virus and threat protection page says the protection is out of date
no third-party antivirus is installed
a scan will be run right after the change

answer.item: Updating the Microsoft Defender Antivirus definitions

appliesWhen: the antivirus engine is running but its threat signatures are old
explanation: An antimalware engine is only as good as its latest definitions. Defender gets new definitions and engine updates through Windows Update, or from Check for updates in Virus and threat protection.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Core 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: let a video-conferencing program accept incoming calls while the host firewall stays on
clues: the program fails only when the firewall is on
the firewall must stay on for the private and public profiles
the program is installed in the usual Program Files folder
the user does not know which ports the program listens on

answer.item: Allowing the app through Microsoft Defender Firewall

appliesWhen: one known program needs incoming connections and its ports do not matter
explanation: By default the firewall blocks unsolicited inbound connections. Adding the program in Allowed apps makes an exception for that program only, so the rest of the PC stays protected.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

need: let an inventory server on a workstation accept connections on TCP 8443 only from the office subnet
clues: only one TCP port must be opened
connections from any other address range must still be blocked
the rule must apply to the domain profile only
the technician has administrator rights

answer.item: Creating an inbound port rule in Defender Firewall with Advanced Security

appliesWhen: a single port must be opened with a limited scope of source addresses
explanation: Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security (wf.msc) can create inbound rules by program, port, or custom settings. A custom scope limits which remote addresses the rule allows.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Core 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: create an account for a new cashier who will only use the point-of-sale and email programs
clues: the cashier must not install programs
the cashier must not change system-wide settings
the cashier needs full use of their own files and profile
the principle of least privilege applies
appliesWhen: a person needs everyday use of the PC without administrative rights
explanation: A standard user (a member of the Users group) owns their own data but cannot install software or change system-wide settings by default. Least privilege says users get no more rights than their work needs.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

need: give a second IT technician the rights to install software, change any setting, and take ownership of files
clues: the technician supports every PC in the branch
the technician must be able to change permissions on any folder
the existing account cannot be shared for security reasons
appliesWhen: a person must have full control of the operating system
explanation: Members of the Administrators group have full control of Windows, including installing software and taking ownership. Because of that power, only people who need it should get this account type.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

need: give a visiting vendor short-term use of a PC with no access to anyone's data
clues: the vendor needs the PC for one afternoon
the vendor must not install software or hardware
the vendor must not be able to change the account password
the account is turned off again when the visit ends
appliesWhen: a temporary visitor needs very limited, short-term use of the PC
explanation: The Guest account gives limited, temporary access and cannot install software, change settings, or reach other users' data. It is disabled by default and should be turned off again after use.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

need: sign in to a new laptop so that her settings and OneDrive files follow her to her other Windows devices
clues: she already uses Outlook.com email
she also has a Windows desktop at home
she wants to buy apps from the Microsoft Store
she wants online password recovery if she forgets her password
appliesWhen: settings, files, and store apps must sync across several devices
explanation: A Microsoft account is linked to an online profile and syncs settings and OneDrive files across devices. It also gives access to the Microsoft Store and online password recovery.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Core 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: set up a kiosk PC with an account that is not linked to any online profile
clues: the kiosk has no email address assigned to it
nothing on the kiosk may sync to other devices
the account must live only on this one PC
the PC was set up without an Internet connection
appliesWhen: an account must exist only on one PC with no online services or sync
explanation: A local account lives only on that PC and is not linked to Microsoft online services. Its data and settings do not sync to other devices.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

need: add an account to the legacy group that an old in-house program checks for when it starts
clues: the program was written for Windows XP
the program refuses to run unless the user is in that older group
the group gives no more rights than a standard user in Windows 11
the user must not become an administrator
appliesWhen: an older application expects a legacy group that exists only for backward compatibility
explanation: The Power Users group is kept in current Windows only for backward compatibility with older programs. Since Windows 7 it has no more rights than the standard Users group.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Core 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: sign in quickly with a short code that would be useless to a thief on any other device
clues: the laptop has no camera or fingerprint reader
the user finds a long complex password hard to type many times a day
the code must be tied to this laptop's hardware
appliesWhen: a short code tied to one device is wanted and no biometric hardware is present
explanation: A Windows Hello PIN is tied to the device it was set up on, so a captured code does not work anywhere else. It needs no camera or fingerprint reader.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

need: sign in without touching the keyboard while wearing gloves
clues: the laptop has an infrared depth-sensing camera
the user's hands are often busy or gloved
the user wants a biometric, passwordless sign-in
appliesWhen: the device has an infrared camera and a hands-free biometric sign-in is wanted
explanation: Windows Hello can sign a user in by face when the device has an infrared camera for depth sensing. The biometric data is protected by the TPM.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

need: sign in with a quick touch instead of typing a password
clues: the laptop has a built-in biometric reader next to the touchpad
the laptop has no infrared camera
the user wants a passwordless method based on something they are
appliesWhen: the device has a fingerprint reader and a touch-based biometric sign-in is wanted
explanation: Windows Hello fingerprint sign-in uses a built-in or USB biometric reader. It is passwordless and based on something the user is.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

need: let staff reach the PC, email, and cloud file storage after signing in only once
clues: users complain about remembering many passwords
the cloud apps trust the company's identity service
the PCs are joined to the company domain
appliesWhen: one sign-in must give access to many systems and applications
explanation: Single sign-on lets one set of credentials reach all the systems a user needs, because the resources trust the first authentication. Its weakness is that one stolen sign-in opens every resource.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Core 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: sign in to any of forty shared lab desktops with the same credentials
clues: the desktops have no cameras or biometric readers
students move to a different desktop every class
a code tied to one device's hardware would not work on the others
the policy requires long, complex secrets
appliesWhen: the same credentials must work on many shared PCs that have no biometric hardware
explanation: A username and password is the traditional sign-in and works on any PC the account can use. It should be long and complex because it can be stolen and reused.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

need: remove a group's access from one subfolder when that access comes from the parent folder
clues: the group's entry is greyed out on the subfolder's Security tab
the parent folder must keep its current permissions
the technician wants to keep the other entries as explicit permissions
appliesWhen: a subfolder must stop receiving permissions from its parent folder
explanation: Inherited permissions cannot be changed on the child folder itself. Disabling inheritance lets the technician convert them to explicit entries and then remove the one that is not wanted.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

need: make every subfolder under a project folder use the project folder's permissions again
clues: several subfolders were given their own explicit entries over the years
the parent folder's entries are correct
all files and folders below must end up matching the parent

answer.item: Replace all child object permission entries with inheritable entries from this object

appliesWhen: permissions must be pushed down to every file and subfolder, overwriting their own entries
explanation: This option in Advanced Security Settings propagates the parent's inheritable permissions to all child objects. It replaces explicit entries further down, so it should be used with care.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Core 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: stop staff from saving changes over a shared form template while still letting them open it
clues: staff open the template many times a day
changes must be saved as a new file instead
the setting is a checkbox on the General tab of the file's properties
appliesWhen: a file must open normally but must not be overwritten
explanation: When the Read-only attribute is set, nobody can save changes to that file, but the changes can be saved as a new file. It is set on the General tab of the file's properties or with attrib.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Core 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: see pagefile.sys and bootmgr in File Explorer while troubleshooting
clues: the files exist but do not appear in the folder listing
they are system files that Windows protects
the change is made on the View tab of File Explorer Options

answer.item: Show hidden files and clear Hide protected operating system files

appliesWhen: hidden and protected system files must be visible in File Explorer
explanation: Protected system files stay invisible until both hidden files are shown and the Hide protected operating system files box is cleared. This is done on the View tab of File Explorer Options.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

need: let the family's administrator account run with limited rights day to day but approve system changes when needed
clues: the parent's account is in the Administrators group
malware should not get full rights silently
a prompt should appear before a program changes the system
the feature is built into Windows
appliesWhen: programs must ask for approval before they get administrative rights
explanation: UAC runs even administrators with a standard token and prompts before giving the full administrative token. This supports least privilege and blocks silent changes by malware.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Core 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: protect everything on a laptop's internal drive if the laptop is lost or stolen
clues: the laptop runs Windows 11 Pro
the motherboard has a TPM chip
the drive must stay unreadable if it is put in another computer
the user should not notice the protection after it is set up
appliesWhen: a whole internal drive must be encrypted as data at rest
explanation: BitLocker encrypts an entire volume and is transparent to the user once it is set up. Its keys are kept in the TPM, so the drive cannot be read in another system.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

need: turn on full-drive encryption on older Windows 11 Pro laptops that have no TPM chip
clues: the encryption wizard reports that no TPM was found
the laptops cannot be replaced this year
the motherboards have no chip to hold the keys

answer.item: Storing the BitLocker startup key on a USB flash drive

appliesWhen: BitLocker is wanted on a computer without a TPM
explanation: BitLocker needs either a TPM or a USB flash drive to hold its keys. Without a TPM, the startup key goes on a USB drive that must be present at boot.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

need: encrypt a USB flash drive that staff use to carry patient files between sites
clues: the flash drive could be lost on the way
staff must unlock the drive with a password on other Windows PCs
the whole removable drive must be encrypted, not just some files
appliesWhen: a removable drive must be fully encrypted
explanation: BitLocker To Go uses the same encryption as BitLocker on removable drives such as USB flash drives. Windows asks for the drive's password when it is inserted.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Core 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: encrypt a few folders on a shared PC so that other users who sign in to it cannot read them
clues: only three folders hold the sensitive files
the PC has no TPM chip
the drive is formatted with NTFS
the user is a standard user, not an administrator
appliesWhen: only some files or folders on an NTFS volume must be encrypted for one user
explanation: EFS encrypts individual files and folders on NTFS with a certificate stored in the user's profile. It needs no special hardware and any user can turn it on, while BitLocker encrypts a whole volume and needs an administrator.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Core 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: require longer passwords for the developers than for the rest of the domain
clues: the developers' accounts are in the default Users container
the default domain policy must stay as it is for everyone else
the developers and their computers should be managed as one department

answer.item: Moving the developers into an OU and linking a GPO to it

appliesWhen: different policy settings must apply to one department only
explanation: An organizational unit groups users and computers, often by department. A Group Policy Object linked to that OU applies its rules only to the objects inside it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

need: map the same department drives and printers for each user automatically every time they sign in
clues: the tasks must run at sign-in, not at startup
a batch or PowerShell file is placed in the NETLOGON share
the setting is in User Configuration of a GPO
appliesWhen: commands must run automatically each time a user signs in to the domain
explanation: A log-in script runs tasks such as mapping drives when the user signs in to the domain. It is assigned on the account's Profile tab or in the Scripts (Logon/Logoff) section of a GPO.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

need: make each user's documents save to a central file server no matter which domain PC they use
clues: the documents are backed up only on the server
users move between PCs during the week
each user should see the same drive letter for their own folder

answer.item: Connecting the home folder to a network drive (folder redirection)

appliesWhen: a user's documents must be stored centrally on a server share
explanation: On the account's Profile tab, Connect maps the home folder to a network drive such as Z: pointing at the user's folder on a server. This is folder redirection, so documents stay central on any PC.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

need: keep a user's desktop, Start menu, and settings the same on every domain computer they sign in to
clues: the user works at a different desk each day
the settings, not just the documents, must follow the user
the profile path field on the account is empty
appliesWhen: a user's profile settings must follow the user from one domain PC to the next
explanation: A roaming profile is stored on a server share named in the account's profile path. The domain loads it on any PC the user signs in to, so the settings follow the user.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

need: give 40 accounting staff access to the finance share without editing each account
clues: new accounting staff join every month
access must be removed simply when someone leaves the department
the permissions are set once on the share and NTFS folder

answer.item: Adding the users to a security group and granting the group access

appliesWhen: many users need the same access to a resource
explanation: Security groups let a domain admin set permissions once for the group and control access by membership. New users then get access by being added to the group.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

clues: the user gets Access denied when saving to a shared folder over the network
the user can open and read files in that folder
the NTFS permissions give the user Full Control
the Sharing tab shows the Everyone group with Read only

answer.cause: The Read share permission is more restrictive than the NTFS permissions
answer.action: Give the user's group Change or Full Control in the share permissions

firstStep: Compare the share permissions and the NTFS permissions for the user's groups
appliesWhen: the share and NTFS permissions differ and the share level is the more restrictive one
explanation: When both share and NTFS permissions apply over the network, the more restrictive of the two wins. Read at the share level limits the user to Read even with NTFS Full Control.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

clues: one user cannot open a project folder that the rest of the team uses
the user is a member of the team's group, which has Modify
the user is also in a contractors group
the Security tab shows a checked box in the Deny column for the contractors group

answer.cause: An explicit Deny on one of the user's groups overrides the Allow from the other group
answer.action: Remove the Deny entry or take the user out of the contractors group

firstStep: Check the folder's effective permissions for that user
appliesWhen: an explicit Deny on a user or group is blocking access that another group allows
explanation: NTFS permissions from several groups add up, but a Deny always wins over an Allow. Removing the Deny or the membership restores the access.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Core 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

clues: sfc /scannow says it must be run by an administrator in a console session
the user's account is in the Administrators group
the command prompt was opened from Start in the normal way
no UAC prompt appeared when the window opened

answer.cause: The command prompt is running with the standard user token, not elevated
answer.action: Open Command Prompt with Run as administrator and accept the UAC prompt

appliesWhen: an administrator's tool was started without elevated rights
explanation: UAC gives administrators a standard token until a program is started with Run as administrator. Only the elevated window has the administrative token that tools such as sfc need.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Core 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

clues: the user cannot install a new PDF editor
a prompt asks for an administrator's user name and password
the user's account is only in the Users group
other users with IT accounts can install it

answer.cause: The user has a standard account, which cannot install software
answer.action: Have an administrator enter credentials at the prompt or install the program

firstStep: Check which group the user's account belongs to
appliesWhen: a standard user tries to do an administrative task such as installing software
explanation: By default, standard users cannot install software or make system-wide changes. UAC asks for administrator credentials, so an administrator must approve or do the install.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 45: Windows Security Settings

clues: the owner wants to encrypt the whole internal drive
the laptop has a TPM 2.0 chip
the drive encryption applet is missing from Control Panel
the System > About page shows Windows 11 Home

answer.cause: Windows 11 Home does not include BitLocker
answer.action: Upgrade the laptop to Windows 11 Pro and then turn on BitLocker

firstStep: Check the Windows edition in System > About
appliesWhen: the Windows edition does not include the needed security feature
explanation: BitLocker is only in editions such as Pro, Pro for Workstations, Enterprise, and Education. Upgrading to Pro adds it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Core 2 – Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

clues: the option to join a local Active Directory domain is not offered
other company laptops join the domain without trouble
the laptop was bought at a retail store
the domain name and an admin account are correct

answer.cause: The laptop runs Windows Home, which cannot join an Active Directory domain
answer.action: Upgrade the laptop to Windows Pro and then join it to the domain

firstStep: Check the Windows edition in System > About
appliesWhen: the computer runs an edition of Windows that cannot be domain joined
explanation: No Home edition of Windows can connect to Active Directory. An edition such as Pro or Enterprise is needed before the PC can join the domain.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 38: Windows Networking

clues: joining the domain fails with a message that the domain controller cannot be contacted
the PC can browse the Internet
ipconfig shows a public DNS server address
the domain name was typed correctly

answer.cause: The PC is using a DNS server that cannot find the domain controller
answer.action: Set the PC's DNS server to the domain's DNS server and join again

firstStep: Run ipconfig /all to check which DNS server the PC uses
appliesWhen: the PC cannot locate the domain controller by name
explanation: A PC finds the domain controller through the domain's DNS server. A public DNS server cannot answer for an internal domain, so the join fails until DNS points to the domain's server.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 38: Windows Networking

steps.done: quarantined the infected system

need: make sure the infection cannot come back from a saved snapshot during the cleanup
clues: the laptop runs Windows 11 Home
the malware is confirmed and the laptop is off the network
the cleanup has not started yet
attackers often turn System Protection on to keep a foothold
appliesWhen: the PC is quarantined and the cleanup is about to start, so old restore points must not keep the malware
explanation: Restore points made while the PC was infected can bring the malware back. Turning System Restore off and deleting the points comes after quarantine and before remediation.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 51: SOHO Security

need: keep a confirmed infection from reaching the other PCs and the shared drives
clues: the antivirus has just confirmed a worm on the PC
the PC maps two shared folders on the file server
the cleanup will take most of the afternoon

answer.item: Disconnect the PC from the network

appliesWhen: an infection is confirmed and it could spread to other systems
explanation: Quarantine comes right after the symptoms are verified. Removing the network connection stops the malware from spreading or sending data out.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 51: SOHO Security

need: run a removal scan on a PC whose malware closes the scanner as soon as it starts in normal Windows
clues: the anti-malware definitions were updated a minute ago
the PC still boots to the Windows desktop
the scanner closes a few seconds after it opens
appliesWhen: the malware stops the scanner while Windows runs normally but Windows still boots
explanation: Safe Mode loads only the basic drivers and services, so most malware does not start with it. The scanner can then run and remove the files.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 51: SOHO Security

need: scan a drive whose malware loads before Windows and hides its own files
clues: scans inside Windows report no threats
netstat shows a process that calls out to an unknown server
the infection is believed to be a rootkit

answer.item: Scan offline from a preinstallation environment

appliesWhen: the malware hides from any scan that runs inside the infected Windows
explanation: A preinstallation environment or the Microsoft Defender Offline scan boots outside the installed Windows. The rootkit is not running then, so the scanner can see its files.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

need: give the scanner the best chance to detect a threat that was first seen this week
clues: the PC has been off the internet for a month
the threat is a new variant
the scan is about to start
appliesWhen: the scanner's signatures are old and the scan has not been run yet
explanation: A scanner can only find what its definitions describe. Updating the anti-malware software is the first part of remediation, before the scan and removal.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 51: SOHO Security

need: return a PC to a known clean state after every removal tool has failed
clues: scans in Safe Mode and offline scans did not remove the infection
the malware comes back after each reboot
the user's files are already backed up

answer.item: Reimage the drive and reinstall Windows

appliesWhen: all scan and removal methods have failed and the infection persists
explanation: Reimaging or reinstalling is the last resort of remediation. It removes even persistent malware because the drive starts again from a clean image.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 51: SOHO Security

need: give a newly cleaned Windows Home PC a safe point to roll back to after future problems
clues: the last scan found no threats
scheduled scans and updates are already set up
the restore feature is still turned off from the cleanup

answer.item: Enable System Restore and create a restore point

appliesWhen: the system is clean and there is no fallback point yet
explanation: Once the system is clean, System Restore is turned back on and a new restore point is made. It is the step just before educating the user.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

need: lower the chance that the user lets the same threat in again
clues: the infection came from an attachment in a fake invoice email
the PC is clean and protected again
every technical step of the cleanup is finished

answer.item: Educate the user about the threat

appliesWhen: the technical work is done and the user's actions caused the infection
explanation: User education is the final step of the procedure. The user learns what led to the infection and what to look for next time.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 51: SOHO Security

need: keep a cleaned home PC protected after the technician leaves
clues: the malware has just been removed
the user never runs scans by hand
the operating system has missed several patches

answer.item: Schedule scans and turn on automatic updates

appliesWhen: the malware is gone and the PC needs ongoing protection
explanation: Regular scans and updates lower the chance of a new infection. Scans can be scheduled in the anti-malware program or in Task Scheduler.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

need: be sure that a slow PC is really infected before making any major changes
clues: a process named regsvr32.exe is very busy
the user only says the PC feels slow
no antivirus alert has appeared

answer.item: Investigate the symptoms with Process Explorer and netstat

appliesWhen: malware is only suspected and nothing has been confirmed yet
explanation: The first step is to investigate and verify that malware causes the symptoms. Process Explorer and netstat -nab show which processes run and which ones open network connections.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

need: keep the files on the sales team's laptops unreadable if a laptop is stolen
clues: the laptops run Windows 11 Pro
the laptops have a TPM chip
the whole drive must be protected, not only some folders
appliesWhen: the data on a Windows drive must stay protected if the device is lost or stolen
explanation: BitLocker encrypts the whole volume, which is data-at-rest encryption. A thief who removes the drive cannot read the files without the key.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 48: Workstation Best Practices

need: stop users from choosing short passwords that are easy to crack
clues: the computers are not in a domain
current NIST guidance puts length ahead of complexity
many users now choose six-character passwords
appliesWhen: every new password must have at least a set number of characters
explanation: Minimum password length sets how many characters every password must have. Current NIST guidance says longer passwords protect better than forced character rules.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 48: Workstation Best Practices

need: stop users from going back to one of their last few passwords when a change is required
clues: users switch between two favorite passwords
the policy must remember the last five passwords
the minimum password age is set above zero days
appliesWhen: users must not use their recent passwords again
explanation: Enforce password history keeps a list of earlier passwords that cannot be used again. It only works when the minimum password age is above 0 days.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 48: Workstation Best Practices

need: make each password stop working after a set number of days
clues: the clinic's policy requires password expiration
the PCs are standalone and not in a domain
the default is 42 days
appliesWhen: passwords must expire and be changed after a fixed time
explanation: Maximum password age sets how long a password can be used before it must be changed, which is password expiration. NIST now suggests changes only after a suspected breach, but the setting is still used.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 48: Workstation Best Practices

need: require passwords that mix uppercase letters, lowercase letters, digits, and symbols
clues: users choose passwords made only of lowercase words
the auditor wants three of four character types
the setting is under Account Policies
appliesWhen: passwords must contain several different character types
explanation: This policy makes each password meet three of four character groups: uppercase, lowercase, digits, and special characters. It is set in secpol.msc under Account Policies and Password Policy.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 48: Workstation Best Practices

need: stop someone from guessing a user's password with many tries in a row
clues: the event log shows hundreds of failed sign-ins on one account
the account should be blocked for 30 minutes after five bad tries
the setting is under Account Policies
appliesWhen: an account must be blocked after a number of invalid sign-ins
explanation: The account lockout threshold locks the account after a set number of invalid logons. The lockout duration and the reset counter are set in the same Account Lockout Policy.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 48: Workstation Best Practices

need: stop students from changing the boot order to start the lab PCs from their own USB drives
clues: students can open the firmware setup with a key press at startup
the PCs must still start Windows without a password
the change must hold even if Windows is reinstalled
appliesWhen: the firmware setup itself must be protected from changes
explanation: A supervisor password protects the BIOS/UEFI setup utility, so settings such as the boot order cannot be changed without it. A system password would instead block every startup.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 48: Workstation Best Practices

need: make a password necessary before a laptop even starts to load the operating system
clues: the laptops carry engineering drawings
an attacker could boot from other media
the prompt must appear before Windows starts
appliesWhen: nobody may boot the computer at all without a password
explanation: The BIOS/UEFI system password is asked for at startup, before any operating system loads. It stops unauthorized boots, while a supervisor password only protects the setup utility.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 48: Workstation Best Practices

need: make sure an unattended PC asks for a password after a few idle minutes
clues: staff often walk away without locking the PC
patient records are open on the screen
the setting must lock the PC even when the user forgets
appliesWhen: a PC must lock itself after it has been idle for a while
explanation: With On resume, display logon screen checked, the screen saver locks the session after the idle time. The user must sign in again when coming back.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 48: Workstation Best Practices

need: keep a laptop at a busy front desk from being carried away
clues: the laptop sits on an open counter all day
the desk has a solid anchor point
the laptop has a security slot on its side

answer.item: Securing the laptop with a cable lock

appliesWhen: critical hardware must be physically fastened so it cannot be taken
explanation: Securing critical hardware is an end-user best practice. A cable lock ties the laptop to the desk, while encryption only protects the data after a theft.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 48: Workstation Best Practices

need: keep a different long password for each of 40 work websites without writing them down
clues: the user keeps passwords on a sticky note under the keyboard
the user now reuses one password on many sites
the passwords must sync to the user's phone
appliesWhen: many unique, strong passwords must be stored and generated safely
explanation: A password manager such as Bitwarden or 1Password generates and stores a unique strong password for every account. It removes the need to write passwords down or reuse them.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 48: Workstation Best Practices

need: keep an employee from installing software and changing system settings on a shared PC
clues: the employee's account is in the Administrators group
the employee only needs the office apps
the company follows least privilege

answer.item: Making the account a standard user

appliesWhen: a user has more permissions than the job needs
explanation: Restricting user permissions follows the principle of least privilege. A standard user cannot install software or change system settings without an administrator.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 48: Workstation Best Practices

need: allow a domain user to sign in only from 8 in the morning to 6 in the evening on weekdays
clues: the user works a fixed day shift
after-hours sign-ins to this account have been seen
the computers are joined to a Windows domain

answer.item: Setting logon hours on the account

appliesWhen: a user may sign in only at certain hours or days
explanation: In a domain, the Logon Hours button on the account's Account tab sets the hours when the user may log on. Sign-ins outside those hours are refused.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 48: Workstation Best Practices

need: make a contractor's account stop working on the last day of a three-month contract
clues: the contract ends on a known date
the help desk might forget to disable the account by hand
the PC runs Windows 11 Pro
appliesWhen: a temporary account must turn off by itself on a known date
explanation: An account expiration date disables the account automatically on the chosen day. It is set on the account's Account tab, for example in lusrmgr.msc on Windows 11 Pro.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 48: Workstation Best Practices

need: make sure no one can sign in to the PC without a personal account
clues: an audit found a built-in account that needs no password
built-in accounts cannot be deleted
visitors sometimes use the front-office PC
appliesWhen: a built-in account lets people sign in without their own credentials
explanation: The Guest account and other unneeded accounts should be disabled in Local Users and Groups. Built-in accounts cannot be deleted, so they are disabled instead.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 48: Workstation Best Practices

need: make it harder for an attacker to guess the name and password of the built-in full-control account
clues: attack tools try the default account name first
the built-in account has a weak password
the account must stay available for emergencies

answer.item: Renaming the Administrator account and giving it a strong password

appliesWhen: the default administrator account keeps its well-known name or password
explanation: Renaming the default Administrator account and setting a strong password removes the name and password attackers expect. It is done in Computer Management under Local Users and Groups.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 48: Workstation Best Practices

need: stop programs on USB drives and discs from starting by themselves when they are inserted
clues: users bring in USB sticks from home
the media must be scanned before anything runs
the setting is under Bluetooth & devices in Settings or in gpedit.msc
appliesWhen: removable media must not launch anything until it is scanned
explanation: With AutoPlay off, removable media cannot start its AutoRun program, so embedded malware has no chance to run before a scan. The Group Policy setting is named Turn off AutoPlay.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 48: Workstation Best Practices

need: shrink the attack surface of a PC by stopping background features it never uses
clues: the PC runs several services nobody needs
each extra service is a possible way in
the change is made in services.msc
appliesWhen: background services run that the computer does not need
explanation: Setting unneeded services to Disabled reduces the attack surface and frees memory and CPU. Unknown services should be researched first, because some are critical.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 48: Workstation Best Practices

need: make the data on a lost phone unreadable even if the thief gets past the lock screen
clues: the phone may be out of range when a wipe is sent
the phones hold patient notes
the data must be protected while it is stored
appliesWhen: stored data must stay unreadable without the correct passcode
explanation: Device encryption makes the stored data unreadable without the correct passcode. It still protects the data when a remote wipe cannot reach the device.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 49: Mobile Device Security

need: let a user open the phone quickly with a finger while keeping it locked to anyone else
clues: the user keeps the phone unlocked because typing a code is slow
the phone has a fingerprint sensor
a basic swipe gives no protection
appliesWhen: the device needs a fast unlock method that only its owner can use
explanation: A fingerprint or facial recognition lock is based on something the user is. It is quick to use and far stronger than a swipe, which has no security.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 49: Mobile Device Security

need: make the phones lock themselves as soon as possible after they are put down
clues: the phones already require a PIN
the data on them is confidential
the phones stay unlocked for five minutes when idle

answer.item: Setting the screen timeout to its lowest value

appliesWhen: an idle device must lock itself very quickly
explanation: The screen timeout sets how long the device waits before it locks. In a confidential setting it can be set to the lowest value, such as 10 or 15 seconds.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 49: Mobile Device Security

need: apply the same passcode rules, VPN, and app limits to 60 new iPads at once
clues: the devices are already enrolled in the management server
every device must get identical settings
the settings must be built once as a template
appliesWhen: one set of security settings must be pushed to many enrolled devices
explanation: A configuration profile is a set of rules and settings that MDM pushes to the devices. It can restrict app installs, require strong passwords, and set up VPN access.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: close a security hole that the phone's vendor has just patched
clues: a notification says a security patch is ready
the phone is several versions behind
the hole is in the operating system itself
appliesWhen: the operating system has a known flaw that a vendor patch fixes
explanation: Patch management keeps the mobile OS current, and security patches make up a large part of system updates. On iOS they are under Settings, General, Software Update.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 49: Mobile Device Security

need: fix a known flaw in the banking app the user installed last year
clues: the store shows pending updates for several apps
the phone's operating system is current
automatic updates are turned off in the store

answer.item: Updating the apps from the app store

appliesWhen: an installed app is out of date and has a known flaw
explanation: An out-of-date app can be a serious security risk even on a current OS. Apps are updated from the App Store or Google Play, and both can update apps automatically.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 49: Mobile Device Security

need: detect and block malicious apps on Android phones the way it is done on the office PCs
clues: the users sometimes sideload apps
the phone's OS updates are already installed
updates alone do not target viruses
appliesWhen: a device needs protection that finds and removes viruses and other malware
explanation: Endpoint security software for mobile devices includes antivirus and anti-malware apps. Updates fix flaws, but they are not made to fight malware.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 49: Mobile Device Security

need: keep students' tablets from opening adult and gambling websites
clues: the tablets are used by young students
the school must block certain web categories
the tablets already have current updates
appliesWhen: certain kinds of web content must be blocked on the device
explanation: Content filtering is part of mobile endpoint security software. It blocks websites by category or by list.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 49: Mobile Device Security

need: see on a map where a phone was left after a business trip
clues: the phone has location services turned on
the user thinks it was left in a taxi
the user hopes to get the phone back with its data

answer.item: Using a locator app such as Find My

appliesWhen: a missing device must be tracked to find out where it is
explanation: A locator app such as Google Find My Device or Apple Find My shows where the device is when its location service is on. The user can then decide whether to involve the police.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 49: Mobile Device Security

need: make sure a stolen phone with client files can no longer give anyone those files
clues: the phone was taken from a car an hour ago
the phone is still connected to the cellular network
the files are backed up in the cloud
the user has no hope of getting it back
appliesWhen: a lost or stolen device still online must have its data erased from a distance
explanation: A remote wipe deletes the contents of the device from another computer or an MDM server. It works only while the device can reach the internet.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 49: Mobile Device Security

need: make sure the photos and settings on a phone can be restored to a new phone if it is lost
clues: the user has never connected the phone to a computer
the data should be copied regularly
a wipe would otherwise lose everything

answer.item: Turning on cloud backup such as iCloud or Google One

appliesWhen: the device's data must be copied regularly to a safe off-device location
explanation: Remote backup apps such as iCloud and Google One copy data, photos, and settings to the cloud. The data can then be restored after a loss or a wipe.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 49: Mobile Device Security

need: erase the iPhone's data automatically if someone keeps guessing the passcode
clues: the phone is often used in public places
the data on it is sensitive
a recent backup is always kept in iCloud

answer.item: Turning on the erase data option after 10 failed passcode attempts

appliesWhen: the device must wipe itself after repeated wrong passcodes
explanation: This failed log-in restriction wipes the local data after 10 wrong passcodes in a row. It suits users with sensitive data when a recent backup is always available.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: push updates and security settings to 500 company phones from one console
clues: the phones are a mix of Android and iOS
the IT team must be able to lock or wipe any phone
the company has only two mobile admins
appliesWhen: many mobile devices must be secured and managed from one central place
explanation: MDM software secures, monitors, and manages mobile devices from a central server. It can push updates and settings to hundreds of devices at once.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 49: Mobile Device Security

need: let staff read work email on their own phones while keeping company data apart from their personal data
clues: the company allows bring your own device
employees worry about their privacy
company data must be removable when someone leaves

answer.item: Separating work apps and data in a managed container

appliesWhen: personal devices must keep work data separate from personal data
explanation: In a BYOD setting, MDM can put the work apps and data in a separate container. The company can then remove its own data without touching the user's personal files.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 49: Mobile Device Security

need: give staff phones that the company owns and controls but that they may also use for personal calls
clues: the company wants full control of the hardware
staff should not have to carry two phones
the company will buy and prepare each phone
appliesWhen: the organization owns and prepares the device but allows personal use
explanation: With COPE, the organization owns the device, prepares it for work, and then allows personal use, much like a company car. BYOD is the reverse: the employee owns the device.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 49: Mobile Device Security

need: let employees use the phones they already own for work to save the cost of new devices
clues: employees already carry their own smartphones
the company does not want to buy phones
a signed user agreement will set the rules
appliesWhen: employees supply their own devices and the company avoids buying them
explanation: A BYOD policy lets staff use their own devices and sets minimum requirements such as OS, patches, and antivirus. MDM helps enforce those requirements.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: let staff pick their work phone from a short list of company-approved models
clues: the company buys the phones
staff want some say in the device they use
the IT team supports only three models
appliesWhen: users choose from a list of devices that the organization approves and provides
explanation: With CYOD, users select a device from an approved list and the organization provides it. The BYOD, CYOD, or COPE policy should also say how company data is recovered when someone leaves.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 49: Mobile Device Security

need: make sure the phones used for patient data are owned by the clinic and used for work only
clues: personal apps are not allowed on the devices
the clinic must track each device by GPS
staff must be told that the devices are tracked

answer.item: Corporate-owned devices for work use only

appliesWhen: the organization owns the device and personal use is not allowed
explanation: Corporate-owned devices give the organization full control of the data and often let it track the device by GPS. Users must be told about the tracking policy.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: make sure nobody can log in to a newly installed router with credentials published online
clues: the router still accepts the admin name and password printed in its manual
lists of factory logins for this model are easy to find on the Internet
this is the first change being made after unboxing the device
a separate user login on the device should also differ from the admin login
appliesWhen: a device still uses the factory login that anyone can look up
explanation: Factory credentials are widely published, so changing the admin password is the first step in securing any router. Renaming the admin account, where the router allows it, also blocks guessing against the known username.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 51: SOHO Security

need: allow only a short list of known hosts to pass through the router and block every other address
clues: the office has only six computers, each with a fixed address
the owner wants a rule list that ends with an implicit deny
traffic from any address not on the list should be dropped
the rules are entered on the router, not on each computer
appliesWhen: access must be limited to hosts with listed IP addresses
explanation: IP filtering compares each packet's address with a rule list on the router and drops anything not explicitly allowed. It works best in a small network where each host has a known address.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: close known security holes in a router that sat in a warehouse for a year before it was installed
clues: the vendor has posted a newer release with security fixes
the change log lists vulnerabilities fixed since the device was built
the device has not yet been configured or put into service
the owner wants this checked again every month or so
appliesWhen: the device's own software is out of date and the vendor has released fixes
explanation: Exploits may be found while a device sits on a shelf, so its firmware is upgraded before it is configured and put into service. Reading the vendor's change log shows what each release fixes.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: keep a child's computer from reaching anything but a few approved websites, and only on weekday afternoons
clues: the computer is picked by its MAC address in the router's settings
only two domain names should be allowed for that computer
a schedule should limit the hours the computer can go online
the rule must still apply if the computer gets a new IP address
appliesWhen: certain users or computers must be kept away from particular websites or kinds of content
explanation: Content filtering, often found in a router's parental controls section, lets the owner choose which domains a computer may reach and when. Because it follows the MAC address, the rule stays in place when the IP address changes.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 51: SOHO Security

need: stop visitors and staff from pressing the reset button or plugging cables into the office router
clues: the router now sits on an open shelf in the waiting area
anyone who can reach it could hold the reset button and return it to factory settings
the office has a small storage room with a lock
there is no server room in the building

answer.item: Move the router into a locked closet or cabinet

appliesWhen: people who should not touch the network device can reach it
explanation: A router that anyone can reach can be reset, stolen, or plugged into, so it belongs in a locked wiring closet or cabinet. If no locked room exists, mounting it high or above a drop ceiling makes it harder to reach.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 51: SOHO Security

need: let Internet users reach the company web server without giving them any path into the internal LAN
clues: the web server must answer requests from the Internet
the accounting PCs must stay unreachable from outside
the router's firewall can place a host in a separate zone
only the web ports should be allowed to that host
appliesWhen: a public-facing server must be reachable from the Internet but kept apart from the internal network
explanation: A screened subnet, also called a DMZ, is a zone between the Internet and the LAN where public servers sit behind firewall rules. Outside users can reach those servers without reaching internal hosts.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: keep the router's login and settings from being read by anyone listening on the network
clues: the router's web page now loads over plain HTTP
the owner sometimes manages the device from a laptop on Wi-Fi
remote management from the Internet is not needed
the router can also be managed with SSH instead of Telnet
appliesWhen: the device's admin interface must be encrypted and limited to trusted locations
explanation: Secure management access makes the router use encrypted protocols such as HTTPS and SSH for its admin interface, so credentials are not sent in plaintext. Limiting management to the internal network blocks attempts from outside.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: stop the wireless network name from revealing the router's brand and the fact that it was never set up
clues: the network still shows the name the vendor set at the factory
a former employee knows the network by its current name
the owner wants a name with mixed letters and numbers
this should be done before wireless is turned on for staff
appliesWhen: the wireless network still uses the vendor's name or a name many outsiders know
explanation: A default network name tells attackers the router model and suggests other defaults were left in place. Renaming it with a less obvious name adds a small layer of protection.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 51: SOHO Security

need: keep the office Wi-Fi out of the list of nearby networks that passers-by see on their phones
clues: every staff device is already connected to the network
new devices can be added by typing the network name by hand
the owner understands this alone is weak protection
the network already uses strong encryption
appliesWhen: the network name should not show up in normal scans after all clients are connected
explanation: With the broadcast turned off, the network does not appear in normal scans, and new clients must enter its name manually. It is weak on its own because sniffers can still find the network.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 51: SOHO Security

need: protect wireless traffic with the strongest protection that the router and all clients support
clues: the router is set to an older mode that uses TKIP
all of the laptops and phones are recent models
the owner wants protection against passphrase-guessing attacks
the access point offers several security modes in a drop-down list
appliesWhen: wireless traffic must be protected with the newest available security mode
explanation: WPA3 is the current Wi-Fi security standard, and its SAE exchange replaces the preshared-key handshake of WPA2-Personal. Older modes such as WEP, WPA, and TKIP are deprecated.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: give visitors Internet access over Wi-Fi without letting them see the office file server or other staff devices
clues: clients waiting for appointments ask for Wi-Fi
visitors only need web access, not internal resources
smart cameras and speakers could also be kept off the main network
visitor access should use a passphrase and expire after a day
appliesWhen: visitors or untrusted devices need Internet access isolated from internal resources
explanation: A guest network gives visitors Internet access while isolating them from internal resources and from clients on the main network. It still needs a passphrase and encryption, and it should be off when no guests are expected.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 51: SOHO Security

need: make sure a laptop plugged into a spare jack on the router gets no network access
clues: four of the router's eight LAN jacks have nothing connected
the cleaning crew can reach the area where the router sits
the router can turn off individual switch ports
company policy says unused jacks must not give access
appliesWhen: spare physical ports could let an unknown device connect
explanation: A disabled port gives no access even if a rogue computer is plugged into it. Most organizations make this a policy for every unused router and switch port.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 51: SOHO Security

need: let customers on the Internet reach a web server on the LAN through the router's public address
clues: the server has the internal address 192.168.0.100
requests to the router's public address on TCP 443 should reach that server
no other inbound traffic should be allowed
the owner wants to set the rule by hand, not let devices create it
appliesWhen: inbound traffic on one external port must reach one internal host and port
explanation: Port forwarding, also called port mapping, sends traffic that arrives on a chosen WAN port to an internal IP address and port. The firewall should allow only the ports that are needed.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 51: SOHO Security

clues: the router's port table lists inbound ports nobody configured
the entries point to a smart camera and a game console
no one has set up any port rules by hand
an outside scan shows those ports open on the public address

answer.cause: UPnP is letting devices open inbound ports on their own
answer.action: Disable UPnP and remove the unwanted port mappings

firstStep: Check the router's port forwarding table and note which device created each entry
appliesWhen: devices on the LAN create port mappings without the owner's approval
explanation: UPnP lets clients ask the router to open and forward ports automatically. If the owner does not need it, turning it off and forwarding ports by hand closes those openings.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

clues: unknown devices keep showing up in the router's client list
the passphrase was changed last week, and strangers joined again
the router was set up many years ago and never changed
the security mode shows WEP

answer.cause: the network uses outdated encryption that can be cracked easily
answer.action: Change the wireless security mode to WPA3, or WPA2 with AES

firstStep: Check the security mode on the router's wireless settings page
appliesWhen: the wireless security mode is an old one such as WEP or WPA with TKIP
explanation: WEP and TKIP can be cracked with common tools, so a new passphrase does not keep intruders out for long. WPA3 or WPA2 with AES replaces them.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

clues: the home security camera's video loads on the LAN
the same camera cannot be reached from a phone on mobile data
the router's firewall is on with its default rules
no rule sends any inbound traffic to the camera

answer.cause: the router has no port forwarding rule for the camera
answer.action: Create a port forwarding rule to the camera's IP address and port

appliesWhen: a service on the LAN must be reached from the Internet and no rule sends traffic to it
explanation: The router's firewall drops inbound traffic that no rule allows, so a device on the LAN is not reachable from outside. A port forwarding rule maps the external port to the device's internal address and port.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

clues: a new laptop does not list the office network among nearby networks
every older device stays connected without trouble
the router's wireless page shows the network is up
the network name was kept off the air on purpose

answer.cause: SSID broadcast is disabled on the router
answer.action: Connect the laptop by typing the network name and passphrase manually

appliesWhen: a new client cannot see a network that is working for every other device
explanation: When the broadcast is off, the network does not appear in scans, but it still works. A new client joins by entering the network name, security type, and passphrase manually.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 51: SOHO Security

need: stop websites from opening extra windows on their own while still letting the bank's site open its statement window
clues: users keep closing small windows that appear over and under the page
one trusted banking site needs to open a second window
the address bar shows a notice when such a window is stopped
site permissions can be changed from the lock icon
appliesWhen: unwanted windows must be stopped, with exceptions for trusted sites
explanation: The pop-up blocker stops pop-ups and pop-unders and is on for all sites by default in Edge and Chrome. A single site can be allowed from the address bar notice or from that site's permissions.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: remove the history, cookies, saved form entries, and download list left on a shared library computer
clues: many people use the same computer during the day
the next user should not see where the last user went
the time range can be set to all time
the option is under Privacy, search, and services in Edge
appliesWhen: stored history, cookies, and form data must be removed from a browser
explanation: Browsing data covers history, download history, cookies, cached files, passwords, autofill data, and site settings. Clearing it removes what earlier sessions left behind.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: see the newest version of a web page that a developer just changed, without losing saved logins or history
clues: the browser keeps showing the old page layout
other computers show the new version of the page
only stored images and files should be removed
cookies and passwords must stay in place
appliesWhen: the browser shows old copies of page files that were stored locally
explanation: The browser stores the files it has rendered so pages load faster. Clearing only the cached images and files makes it download fresh copies of the page.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: check a personal webmail account on a borrowed computer and leave no history, cookies, or logins behind
clues: the computer belongs to a coworker
the session should not use the owner's saved data
everything from the session must be gone when the window closes
the user can open it with Ctrl+Shift+N in Edge or Chrome
appliesWhen: a single session must leave no browsing data on the computer
explanation: Private-browsing mode, called InPrivate in Edge and Incognito in Chrome, stores no browsing data and discards the session's data when the window closes. Extensions are off in it by default.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 52: Browser Security

need: have favorites, history, and saved passwords appear on a new laptop and a phone automatically
clues: the user signs in to the browser with a personal account
the same browser is installed on every device
the user wants nothing copied by hand
a work browser should stay separate from a personal account
appliesWhen: a user wants the same browser data on several devices through a signed-in account
explanation: When the user signs in to the browser and turns on sync, browsing data follows the account to other devices. Personal and work accounts should stay separate, so a personal account is never synced to a work browser.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: stop the banners and sidebar ads on news sites that may lead to adware and track browsing habits
clues: the unwanted content is part of the page, not separate windows
some sites serve malicious ads
the user can allow a site that asks for an exception
the tool is added from the browser's store
appliesWhen: advertising inside web pages must be blocked to reduce tracking and malicious ads
explanation: An ad blocker extension stops most ads on web pages, which cuts tracking and the risk of malicious ads. Sites that depend on ad income can be allowed as exceptions.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 52: Browser Security

need: send all web requests through a company server that filters banned sites and logs requests centrally
clues: management decides which categories of sites are blocked
the server fetches each page for the client and returns it
the setting can be pushed to every computer by policy
the operating system offers a manual setup option and an automatic script option
appliesWhen: web traffic must go through a server that filters, caches, or logs it
explanation: A proxy server fetches web content on behalf of clients, which allows central filtering, caching, and logging. In Windows it is set under Settings > Network & internet > Proxy, often by policy.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: keep anyone on the public network from reading or changing the browser's name lookups
clues: the user often works over coffee shop Wi-Fi
normal lookups are sent in plain text
the user wants to choose a provider such as Cloudflare
the option is in the Security part of the privacy settings
appliesWhen: name lookups must be encrypted to stop eavesdropping and tampering
explanation: Secure DNS, also called DNS over HTTPS, encrypts the browser's DNS queries so others cannot read or alter them. Edge and Chrome let the user keep the current provider or pick a custom one.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: use a long, different password for each of dozens of websites without writing any of them down
clues: the user keeps reusing one password on many sites
a breach at one site could expose the others
the stored entries should be protected by one strong master passphrase
entries should fill in on the right sites automatically
appliesWhen: many unique website credentials must be stored and filled in securely
explanation: A password manager stores each site's credentials in an encrypted vault and fills them in when needed. Unique passwords per site stop a breach at one site from exposing the others.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 52: Browser Security

need: install a second web browser on a new Windows 11 computer without picking up a fake installer
clues: the search results show several download links, some of them ads
malware is often dressed up as browser installers
the vendor publishes the installer on its own site
the address bar should show the vendor's domain

answer.item: Download the installer from the vendor's official website

appliesWhen: software must come from a known, legitimate source
explanation: Installers should come only from the vendor, which the address bar's domain confirms. Links from ads or unknown sites may deliver malware dressed up as the browser.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: confirm that an offline browser installer kept on a file share has not been changed since it was downloaded
clues: a SHA256 value was recorded when the installer was first saved
the file will be used for many future installs
the computer has the built-in PowerShell cmdlets
any mismatch should be treated as an untrusted file

answer.item: Compare the file's hash with Get-FileHash

appliesWhen: a stored file must be checked for tampering against a known value
explanation: A hash is a fixed-length summary of a file, and any change to the file changes it. Running Get-FileHash and comparing the result with the stored value shows whether the installer was altered.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: add a note-taking tool to the browser with the least chance of getting a malicious add-on
clues: a website offers the add-on as a file to load by hand
the same add-on is listed in the vendor's add-on ecosystem
the browser warns about add-ons loaded outside its store
the user wants the add-on to update automatically

answer.item: Install the extension from the browser's official add-on store

appliesWhen: a browser add-on is needed and a vendor-vetted source offers it
explanation: The Chrome Web Store and Edge Add-ons are trusted sources because the vendor vets publishers and delivers updates. Sideloaded add-ons are untrusted and may hold malware.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

need: make sure an online store's connection is encrypted and belongs to the real company before typing in card details
clues: the page asks for a credit card number
the user wants to see who issued the site's certificate
the address should begin with HTTPS
the details can be opened from the address bar

answer.item: Check the padlock and view the site's certificate

appliesWhen: a site's secure connection and identity must be confirmed before sensitive data is entered
explanation: The padlock shows that TLS encrypts the connection, and the certificate details show who it was issued to and by which CA. Users should not enter personal data on a site without a secure connection.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 52: Browser Security

need: make sure every staff browser gets security fixes soon after they are released
clues: users often leave the browser open for weeks
the browser downloads fixes in the background
a notice in the menu asks the user to restart the browser
the administrator can set a deadline by policy

answer.item: Require the browser to relaunch to apply updates

appliesWhen: browser updates are downloaded but are not applied until the browser restarts
explanation: Chrome and Edge download patches silently, but an update is not applied until the browser restarts. A policy that requires a relaunch within a set time makes sure the fixes are applied.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

clues: the browser shows a full-page warning that the connection is not private
the warning appears only on the company's time-tracking site
the site loaded with a padlock until yesterday
the certificate details show a date that has passed

answer.action: Have the site's administrator renew the certificate and do not bypass the warning

firstStep: View the certificate details from the warning page
appliesWhen: a single site shows a certificate warning and its certificate is no longer valid
explanation: Browsers warn when a certificate is expired, revoked, or not issued by a trusted CA. Data should not be entered until the site has a valid certificate.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

clues: the home page and search engine changed without the user's choice
a new toolbar appeared after a free video tool was installed
searches go to an unfamiliar site full of ads
the browser now runs more slowly

answer.cause: an extension from an untrusted source has taken over the browser settings
answer.action: Remove the unknown extension and reset the browser settings

firstStep: Open the browser's extensions page and look for add-ons the user did not choose
appliesWhen: unwanted changes to the home page or search appear after untrusted software was installed
explanation: Extensions from untrusted sources can change settings, collect data, and slow the browser. Removing the unknown add-on and resetting the browser to defaults undoes its changes.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 52: Browser Security

clues: an intranet page still shows last week's menu and broken images
the page looks correct on other computers
the page looks correct in a private window
the user's extensions are all trusted and unchanged

answer.cause: the browser is loading old copies of the page's files from its cache
answer.action: Clear the browser's cached images and files

appliesWhen: a page shows old content only on one browser that has stored copies of its files
explanation: The browser keeps copies of page files to load them faster, and an old copy can hide recent changes. Clearing the cached images and files makes it download the current page.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

clues: a web app's buttons do nothing in the user's normal window
the same web app works in an InPrivate window
several add-ons were installed from the official store last month
clearing the cache did not help

answer.cause: an installed extension interferes with the page
answer.action: Turn off all extensions, then turn them back on one at a time to find the one at fault

appliesWhen: a page breaks only when the user's add-ons are running
explanation: Extensions act on the pages the browser renders, so one can break a site. Private windows run with extensions off by default, which points to an add-on; turning them off and back on one by one finds it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems

clues: a security scan reports a browser version with known flaws
the newer version has already been downloaded
the menu icon shows an update notice
the user has not closed the browser for three weeks

answer.cause: the downloaded update is waiting for the browser to restart
answer.action: Relaunch the browser to apply the pending update

appliesWhen: a browser has a pending update that has not been applied
explanation: Browsers download updates in the background but apply them only when they restart. Until then, the old version and its flaws stay in use.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 6: Securing Operating Systems
